title: Split an eight-card deck
prompt: Use slices to assign the first four cards to `hand` and the remaining four to `queue`. Example: `items[:2]` selects two starting items.
starter:
deck = ["X-Bow", "Tesla", "Ice Wizard", "Knight", "Skeletons", "Tornado", "Rocket", "The Log"]
# TODO: make two four-card lists.
hand = []
queue = []
solution:
deck = ["X-Bow", "Tesla", "Ice Wizard", "Knight", "Skeletons", "Tornado", "Rocket", "The Log"]
hand = deck[:4]
queue = deck[4:]
tests:
assert hand == deck[:4], "hand must contain the first four cards in order"
assert queue == deck[4:], "queue must contain the last four cards in order"
assert len(hand) == len(queue) == 4, "Both groups should contain four cards"

title: Read the real card-name mapping
prompt: The supplied scaffold reads the allowed real identifier mapping. Assign `knight_name = card_names["26000000"]` and `entry_count = len(card_names)`. Example: identifiers are strings, not costs. The count is checked against the file, never a fixed dataset size.
starter:
import json
with open("icebow/data/card_ids.json", encoding="utf-8") as source:
    card_names = json.load(source)
# TODO: inspect the mapping using collection operations.
knight_name = ""
entry_count = -1
solution:
import json
with open("icebow/data/card_ids.json", encoding="utf-8") as source:
    card_names = json.load(source)
knight_name = card_names["26000000"]
entry_count = len(card_names)
tests:
with open("icebow/data/card_ids.json", encoding="utf-8") as check_source:
    expected_mapping = json.load(check_source)
assert isinstance(card_names, dict), "The file should load as a dictionary"
assert card_names == expected_mapping, "Preserve the complete mapping read from disk"
assert knight_name == expected_mapping["26000000"], "Look up the string identifier 26000000 in the real mapping"
assert entry_count == len(expected_mapping), "entry_count should equal the current mapping size"
hint: The scaffold handles reading; your task uses only lookup and len.
